title: From Apparent Search Gains to Selection Failures: Auditing Test-Time Inference in Structured Workflow Planning
abstract: arXiv:2611.00579v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Test-time search can improve structured planning, but when methods differ in prompts, post-processing, and selection, it is unclear what an observed gain should be attributed to. We study this question on DisasterBench, where models compose typed multi-tool workflows, by decomposing inference into three observable stages: whether a correct workflow is discovered, whether it survives structural validation, and whether it is finally selected. translated_title: 从表面的搜索增益到选择的失败：结构化工作流规划中测试时推理的审计
tldr: 该论文将测试时推理审计性地分解为“发现—存留—选中”三个可观测阶段，揭示名义树搜索的收益实际来自其扩展提示词而非真正的搜索结构，且失败主要发生在最终选择环节而非结构验证环节。
en_tdlr: This paper audits test-time inference by decomposing it into three observable stages—discovery, survival, and selection—revealing that nominal tree-search gains stem from its expansion prompt rather than genuine search, and that failures arise mainly at the final selection stage rather than during structural validation.
